c.tagline: Neon skyline where East meets futuristic ambition.

emergency.note: 119 is fire; English-speaking operators are hit-or-miss, so having your hotel call can be faster.

hood_landmark.The Bund: the colonial riverfront promenade facing Pudong's skyline
hood_landmark.Lujiazui: the Oriental Pearl Tower and 632 m Shanghai Tower

avoid.reason: The "tea ceremony"/bar scam around the Bund and Nanjing Rd; pickpocketing

hood_desc: Iconic waterfront promenade along the Huangpu River lined with grand colonial-era buildings and the classic view of Pudong skyscrapers across the water, best for first-time visitors who want landmark sightseeing, luxury riverfront hotels, and postcard skyline views.

Pudong's futuristic financial district bristling with supertall towers like the Shanghai Tower and the Oriental Pearl, ideal for business travelers and anyone wanting modern high-rise hotels, big malls, and dramatic skyline views.

Leafy, tree-lined district of historic villas, boutiques, cafes and wine bars with a relaxed European atmosphere, perfect for travelers who value charm, walkability, and a stylish, low-key neighborhood feel.

Upscale central district around Jing'an Temple mixing office towers, luxury shopping, and strong dining and nightlife, great for those who want convenience, buzz, and excellent metro connections in the heart of Puxi.
Trendy pedestrian enclave of restored shikumen stone-gate houses turned into chic restaurants, bars, and shops, suits visitors chasing nightlife, dining, and a polished cosmopolitan vibe.
lodging: Maxx by Steigenberger on the Bund Shanghai

water.note: Avoid tap water; stick to bottled or boiled water, which is the local norm even for residents.

transit.pay: Since 2025 you can tap a foreign Visa/Mastercard directly at metro gates network-wide (Tap to Ride). Alternatively use QR codes in the Metro Daduhui app or Alipay/WeChat (both accept international cards), or buy single tickets and the rechargeable Shanghai Public Transportation Card at station machines and service counters. Rides cost CNY 3-15 (about US$0.40-2).
transit.hours: Metro runs roughly 5:30am-11pm (varies by line, slightly later on some lines Fri-Sat); no overnight service.

landmarks: Oriental Pearl Tower
The futuristic pink-spheres tower is Shanghai's most iconic skyline silhouette, especially lit up at night.
Shanghai Tower
The twisting 632m supertall skyscraper, one of the world's tallest buildings, dominates the Pudong skyline.
The Bund
A riverside promenade of colonial-era buildings facing the futuristic Pudong skyline, Shanghai's single best photo vantage point.
Yu Garden
A classical Ming-dynasty garden of pavilions, rockeries, and koi ponds tucked amid the old city's bazaar.
Jin Mao Tower
An elegant pagoda-inspired skyscraper with an observation deck offering classic Pudong panoramas.
Nanjing Road
China's busiest shopping street, awash in neon signage, is a vibrant scene for street and night photography.
Shanghai World Financial Center
Nicknamed the 'bottle opener' for its distinctive trapezoidal aperture, a standout in the Pudong skyline.
Jade Buddha Temple
An active Buddhist temple housing serene jade Buddha statues, a colorful contrast to the modern city around it.
Xintiandi
A restored lane-house district of shikumen architecture turned into a stylish dining and shopping quarter, great for atmospheric shots.
Shanghai Museum
A granite building shaped like an ancient bronze ding vessel on People's Square, holding China's finest collection of bronzes, ceramics, jade, and calligraphy.

intl.op: China Railway, Guangzhou-Shenzhen-Hong Kong high-speed rail

train.note: Shanghai has no train to a foreign country, but there is a direct high-speed service from Shanghai Hongqiao to Hong Kong West Kowloon, which although domestic in law is a full immigration crossing with passport and permit checks on arrival. Domestic high-speed trains from Hongqiao and Shanghai stations reach most of China, with Nanjing about 75 minutes, Beijing about 4.5 hours and Hangzhou under an hour. Book on the official 12306 English site or app - ID or passport is required for every ticket and is checked at the gate. Hongqiao is enormous and shares its complex with the airport, so allow a good 30-45 minutes between arriving and boarding.

bus.note: No international coach routes serve Shanghai. Long-distance domestic buses leave from the Shanghai Long-Distance Bus Terminal beside Shanghai Railway Station and from the south bus station, but for almost any journey the train is faster, cheaper to book and far easier for a foreign visitor to arrange. Coaches are mainly useful for water towns and smaller Jiangsu and Zhejiang destinations off the rail network.

ferry.note: The weekly Shanghai-Osaka/Kobe ferries - China-Japan International Ferry's Xin Jian Zhen and Shanghai Ferry Co's Su Zhou Hao - suspended passenger sailings in December 2025 amid China-Japan tensions and had not resumed as of mid-2026, so there is currently no scheduled international sea route. Check the operators' own sites before planning any sea crossing, as these services have been suspended and restored several times. Domestically the only regular boats are short river ferries across the Huangpu between Puxi and Pudong, plus sightseeing cruises on the Bund.

half.name: Suzhou
half.blurb: Famed for its elegant classical gardens, arched stone bridges and tranquil canal-lined old quarters.

half.name: Hangzhou
half.blurb: Beautiful West Lake, pagodas and tea plantations have enchanted poets and travelers for centuries.

half.name: Zhujiajiao
half.blurb: Ancient water town threaded with canals, wooden houses and centuries-old humpbacked stone bridges.

half.name: Wuzhen
half.blurb: One of China's loveliest water towns, with lantern-lit canals and timeworn riverside architecture.

half.name: Zhouzhuang
half.blurb: Picturesque canal town of gabled houses, waterways and gently arching stone footbridges.
